problem: End-to-end RL/IL navigation policies compress all behavior into network weights, so sparse, high-cost events (e.g. human collisions at blind corners) are diluted, and policies cannot adapt to OOD social behavior or sim-to-real shifts after training. Prior retrieval-augmented navigation stores snapshot observations rather than interaction dynamics.
motivation: Social navigation is dominated by rare but costly events, and human behavior at test time differs from simulated training crowds. An explicit non-parametric memory that indexes the precursors of high-advantage events can be retrieved at inference and refilled with test-time experience, adapting without gradient updates.
key_idea: Augment a recurrent PPO navigation agent with a FIFO episodic memory keyed by GRU hidden states from k steps before high-|advantage| events, storing action and a saturated Q-value 'scorecard', retrieved via top-K cosine attention, and refilled online at deployment.
insight: Advantage-driven memory selection also improves the base policy even with memory zeroed (SR 76.16 to 79.60 ID), and the trained memory adds more (81.28). Under OOD the trained buffer helps little (56.40) but the online buffer with rule-based outcome labels reaches 60.00 SR. The critic's predicted value is unreliable OOD (human collisions rise to 4.00), and the choice of query feature (hidden state + orthogonal loss vs. all obs or human features) sets the safety/efficiency trade-off.
method: Base agent: GRU recurrent PPO policy from Janny et al. with RGB, LiDAR, odometry/localization, goal and a Wayformer-style human-trace encoder; 29 discrete velocity actions (incl. an added wait action); fine-tuned with dense reward.

Memory retrieval: the previous hidden state h_{t-1} is projected by a 2-layer MLP f_c; cosine similarity to stored keys, top-K=5, softmax (tau=1) attention gives pooled feature m_hat_t concatenated into the GRU input; orthogonality regularizer on projected states avoids collapse.
Memory entries (Scorecard): m_n = f_m(f_c(h_{t_n-k}) .. E[a_{t_n-k}] .. f_v(Q_bar)), with Q_bar = tanh(V+A) from GAE; k=6 look-ahead stores causal precursors rather than the event state itself.
Offline selection: after each batch of episodes keep the top 5% steps by |GAE advantage| in a FIFO buffer of capacity 512.

Online selection at deployment: replace the GAE surprise by |V_{t+1}-V_t| or by a sparse outcome reward (+1 success, -1 collision/failure/timeout); labels assigned by rule (-1 for critical failures, +1 for success); human curation is also possible; no backprop needed.
Training setup: Habitat-Sim/HM3D PointGoal with Recast-simulated non-reactive crowds, density curriculum 0.05 to 0.2 people/m².

setting.backbone: GRU-based recurrent PPO policy (half-width ResNet, 1D-CNN, Wayformer-style human encoder) with retrieval memory, fine-tuned from Janny et al. weights
setting.training_data: RL in simulation on HM3D with simulated crowds (density curriculum 0.05-0.2), no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + LiDAR-like ranges + odometry and mapping-based localization + polar goal vector + previous action + 2D human position traces
setting.action_space: 28 discrete velocity commands (4 linear x 7 angular) plus a 29th wait action
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D) with Recast Navigation crowd simulation
setting.privileged: Human 2D poses given as input; training reward uses privileged env state; online phase uses only outcome labels (success/collision), no GT map

numbers_note: Custom crowd-navigation benchmark in Habitat/HM3D, not a standard canonical benchmark; HC/EC are per-episode collision counts (labels garbled in the source macros). Baselines without memory: ID SR 76.16, OOD SR 54.00.
results: On in-distribution crowds, memory raises SR from 76.16 (baseline) to 81.28 and SPL from 65.65 to 70.33. Under OOD crowds SR goes from 54.00 (baseline) and 56.40 (trained buffer) to 60.00 with an online buffer, with human collisions falling to 3.24. Query time stays at 0.10-0.125 ms for 512-4096 entries.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation with non-reactive simulated crowds; real-robot tests are future work, and the sim-trained latent query space may keep a sim-to-real gap
Human collisions slightly increase in ID (2.67 to 3.33) and the SR gains are modest; FIFO memory and heuristic online labels are simplistic
Single benchmark, no comparison against other social-navigation or retrieval-augmented methods, no seeds or variance reported
